description:
The site visit will be held on Wednesday, December 2, 2026, at 10:30 a.m. Eastern Standard Time (EST). Quoters who do not attend the  mandatory site visit  will be non-responsive offerors. 

 USDA requires a Design/Build contractor to complete the rehabilitation of Parking Lot 9 at the Jamie L. Whitten Building in Washington, DC. The project includes perimeter security upgrades, parking lot resurfacing, sinkhole remediation, electrical work, and landscaping, and is a key component of a larger effort to establish Level IV security protection around the facility. The contractor must assess and update incomplete 2021 construction documents, verify the suitability of security materials already stored on site, and coordinate closely with WMATA due to the Orange, Blue, and Silver Metro lines running beneath the parking lot. After construction began in 2024, sinkholes developed near a WMATA elevator, halting work; therefore, the contractor must determine the full extent of subsurface issues and implement a remediation plan approved by both USDA and WMATA, incorporating recommendations from Langan’s geotechnical investigation. With historic preservation approvals already secured and no work-hour restrictions in place, the project’s objective is to restore progress on the halted construction and deliver the required Level IV perimeter security enhancements within eleven and a half months of Notice to Proceed (NTP) issuance.
